This study introduces a novel approach to evaluating machine writing assistance by leveraging pre-trained transformer language models. Rather than relying on gold-standard references, our method utilizes a large corpus of problems and solutions from existing writing assistants to generate solution quality assessments. The primary contribution is a straightforward, unsupervised solution grading framework based on these pre-trained models. The proposed system was tested on two writing assistance benchmarks: machine grammar correction and machine paragraph summarization. The results demonstrate that this unsupervised approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art evaluation metrics.

Domain adaptive pedestrian identification (DAPI) addresses the challenge of recognizing pedestrians across different camera views when labeled data is scarce in the target domain. While current state-of-the-art approaches primarily rely on domain alignment to minimize distribution shifts, they often overlook the accumulation of false positives during this process. This paper introduces Box Reordering (BOR), an unsupervised strategy that treats false positive reduction as a subproblem of minimizing misplaced domain alignment through the correction of anchor boxes. By reordering these boxes, the method aligns true positives across domains while simultaneously suppressing mismatches. Empirical results on the Pedestrian Identification dataset demonstrate that integrating BOR with the existing domain adaptive method DAPI-Match yields a 2.5% improvement in mAP, establishing a new state-of-the-art performance.

We propose an end-to-end framework designed to enhance music across diverse genres by applying time-warped transformations to its chroma keyframe image representation. The warped transformations are subsequently translated back into the time-domain via a deep neural network. To synthesize final outputs, the modified color image is combined with the original audio track through synchronous windowing and vocoding techniques. We introduce a novel method for synchronizing audio-visual data and develop a specific library of time-warped transformations. Empirical results demonstrate that our approach significantly elevates the aesthetic quality of music without necessitating any handcrafted feature engineering.

This study examines how inaccurately recorded release points affect performance evaluations in sports like baseball pitching and basketball shooting. Using simulations, the researchers analyzed how errors in these data influence calculated metrics, including release height, release velocity, and launch angle for throws. The results indicate that while average performance remains largely unaffected, the sport's defensive efficiency is significantly compromised by such errors. Specifically, the study found that estimated launch angles and release velocities can deviate by as much as 15° and 10% respectively due to flawed release point placement. Consequently, the authors recommend that sports analytics professionals exercise extreme caution when using throw data that relies on imprecise release point recordings.

Although decoding strategies for machine interpretation have been extensively studied, they have largely overlooked the task's inherent syntactic structure. This paper introduces a new, syntax-driven approach to decoding by utilizing syntactic links to model the task as a tree construction process. Specifically, we propose a method that builds the output tree from the top down, establishing the main constituents first before recursively refining them into finer components. To demonstrate the efficacy of this strategy, we apply it to the challenging task of machine semantic parsing. Experimental results on the challenging AMR dataset reveal that our proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Accurate binding energies are essential for astrochemical models to simulate molecular formation on interstellar dust grains. However, existing calculations often lack the necessary precision and accuracy. To address this, we introduce the Binding Energy Assessment Platform (BEAP), a specialized repository hosting binding energies for diverse atom-surface and molecule-substrate systems. BEAP facilitates the analysis of energy distributions across varying computational methods and theoretical models. By aggregating data from quantum chemistry studies, BEAP offers a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating future binding energy calculations.

This study examines the stochastic multiplicative lognormal model, which is often employed to simulate the population growth of species. The analysis focuses on the consequences of imposing a minimum threshold on sampled estimates of population size—a constraint grounded in biological logic. The findings indicate that such limits introduce a negative bias into the estimates, with the magnitude of this bias intensifying as the cutoff value rises. Furthermore, the bias remains relatively stable across varying population sizes but escalates significantly as the standard deviation increases. The research also highlights that the choice of a specific lognormal distribution parameterization substantially affects both bias and variance. Consequently, it is recommended that researchers utilize the parameterization that directly corresponds to the mean and variance of the underlying population distribution.

We introduce a randomized algorithm designed to estimate the overlap between a quantum state and its closest valid tensor network tensor. This method relies on random Clifford circuits and is capable of running on a digital computer, offering a full approximation of the optimal projection error for any quantum state. We demonstrate that this technique effectively identifies states that deviate from a low-depth tensor network structure. Furthermore, we extend the method to calculate the average overlap of an ensemble of states with a single measurement, significantly enhancing its statistical utility.

This study examines the global behavior of the solution to the reflectionless inverse scattering problem associated with the reflectionless case of the Davey-Stewartson II equations. Specifically, the analysis demonstrates that the vector function $q(x,t) = (u(x,t), v(x,t))$ vanishes asymptotically as $|k|^m$ tends to infinity for every non-negative integer $m$. This asymptotic behavior is established by utilizing the analytic properties of the scattering matrix and the known estimates of the Green's function derived from the Lax pair formulation.

The Sibyl algorithm is a well-known technique for detecting anomalies in social networks. This study introduces Sibylvariant, an adaptation of the algorithm designed to classify texts, particularly those containing typographical errors. By leveraging word embeddings to capture semantic similarity, this approach offers text samples that are alike in meaning. Consequently, Sibylvariant demonstrates superior resilience against deliberate text obfuscation attempts compared to its predecessor.

This work introduces a method for automatically generating linear depictions of scenes from a single image, a capability with applications in augmented reality, virtual reality, and 3D gaming. We frame this as a meta-learning task where a model learns to infer the linear depictions of training images, which are created using known 3D scene geometries and camera parameters. By employing a differentiable renderer, we enable the simultaneous optimization of depiction parameters and the geometry of the scene from the input image. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in predicting 3D scene structures from 2D images, as validated by multiple quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

Neural machine translation (NMT) models are typically large, resource-intensive systems that struggle to operate within the strict memory and computational limits of low-end hardware. Addressing this, techniques like knowledge distillation and quantization have been developed to create smaller, more efficient equivalents of high-performance NMT architectures. Nevertheless, these methods often introduce performance degradation, and their resilience against adversarial attacks remains largely uninvestigated. This study investigates the vulnerability of both quantized and distilled models by subjecting them to white-box and black-box attack scenarios. Our findings indicate that these transformations significantly heighten model susceptibility, revealing that distillation amplifies this risk more than quantization does.

This study introduces a novel Lagrangian function tailored to a solitary hypergraph, from which corresponding Euler equations are derived. Furthermore, we establish a unique hypergraph Ectesian matrix based on a designated weight function and demonstrate that this matrix is positive definite.

Deep learning approaches have proven highly effective for biomedical image segmentation; however, gathering extensive annotated datasets remains a costly and time-consuming endeavor. This paper introduces a strategy to reduce the reliance on labeled data for biomedical image segmentation by leveraging data augmentation through image enhancement techniques. Focusing on a specific task, we examine the segmentation of pneumonia within chest X-rays. Experimental results indicate that a model trained using this proposed method outperforms one trained solely on raw data, demonstrating its efficacy in biomedical segmentation applications.

Conditioned image generation is a prevalent approach for creating handcrafted descriptions using natural language prompts. However, existing models often produce lengthy and structurally complex captions that are difficult to parse and manage. This paper presents a prompting-based strategy aimed at generating concise and straightforward image descriptions. Our method involves training a sequence-to-sequence model to map long, detailed descriptions into compact, simple ones. By leveraging these simplified captions as intermediate references, we can rephrase standard descriptions to maintain their original meaning while adopting a more accessible structure. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed pipeline produces captions that are significantly shorter and contain fewer grammatical constructs compared to prior work, all without compromising the quality of the generated content.

We introduce a new framework for modeling the causal properties of physical objects, which models the causal transfer of a "damage" state from an attacker to a defender. This approach is implemented using a novel automata structure called a causal automata, capable of representing the causal representations of both physical entities and the abstract notion of damage. This formalism is established on the foundation of space-time and the causal flow of information. We demonstrate the utility of this methodology by applying it to verify security guarantees, specifically confidentiality and integrity, within the damage model.

Deep learning has emerged as a highly effective approach for numerous machine learning challenges, particularly when implemented with the MMLSpark library. This paper details a new, extensible deep learning framework designed to scale across distributed environments using MMLSpark. We present the core architectural components and their integration within the MMLSpark ecosystem, alongside the initial framework implementation. The objective is to establish a versatile platform capable of supporting diverse, custom, and new deep learning models.

We introduce an unsupervised framework for "zero-shot" speech-to-speech, capable of handling voice characteristics from unseen speakers without requiring any speech or voice annotations. Our method integrates two components: (1) a "universal" language model trained on a vast corpus of speech from diverse, unlabeled individuals, and (2) a "zero-shot" voice synthesizer that generates a target speaker's voice from their recorded utterances. We demonstrate that this approach enables unsupervised, zero-shot voice cloning and interpretation. Specifically, we trained the universal model using 1.5 million hours of unlabeled audio, allowing it to generalize to entirely new speakers encountered during testing. We further show that the system can perform cross-lingual voice cloning, synthesizing voices from speakers whose language was not present during training. Additionally, we illustrate how this model facilitates voice translation, converting both the content and the unique vocal characteristics of an utterance from one language to another.

This study examines a thermal model characterized by the first-order Coleman-Gurtin heat equation coupled with nonlinear thermal boundary conditions. The term representing heat relaxation is formulated as a nonlinear integral expression, while the boundary conditions for heat flux are defined as a nonlinear function of both temperature and the thermal relaxation component. Utilizing the monotone map technique, we establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions. Furthermore, we demonstrate the smoothness of solutions provided the initial data is sufficiently smooth.

Accurate estimation of peak daily demand is vital for grid operators, particularly when integrating significant amounts of fluctuating renewable energy sources. This study evaluates the performance of various peak demand forecasting models, including those that utilize the entire historical load profile, those that rely on day-type classification, and those that integrate multiple sub-models through forecast combination. The analysis employs daily peak demand data from 120 German low-voltage distribution substations, covering the period between 2015 and 2018. The findings indicate that models combining multiple sub-methods outperform those based solely on load profile analysis or profile classification. Additionally, the research demonstrates that the proposed methods are robust against variations in the spatial distribution of electric vehicle charging behavior.

We introduce a framework designed to embed knowledge from human domain experts into machine learning models. This blueprint outlines the essential steps required to construct a "black-box" machine learning system that effectively synthesizes insights from multiple expert sources. To demonstrate this approach, we applied the framework to a neural network trained for image classification using a curated dataset of COVID-19 chest X-rays, incorporating clinical expertise from physicians.

Accurately positioning vertebrae is essential for spine-related clinical tasks, including the assessment of curvature, deformity, and fracture detection. Although deep learning has recently shown promise in spine analysis, a significant limitation remains: most methods rely on pre-processing steps to align vertebrae before extraction, yet these auxiliary techniques often lack robustness and fail to generalize across different clinical settings. To overcome this, we introduce a new approach that directly and automatically rectifies the spine from CT images using a newly developed convolutional neural network (CNN). This method employs a specialized loss function designed to enhance feature learning along the vertebral longitudinal axis. Additionally, we implemented an anatomically grounded enhancement technique that leverages the inherent structural properties of the spine to further refine CNN performance. Experimental results indicate that our vertebra positioning system outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions.

We investigate the interaction of a single electron with an optical field confined within a cavity. By employing a quantum kinetic approach, we demonstrate that rapid oscillations induced by the oscillatory nature of the electron's scattering amplitude can lead to the electron's dynamical stabilization. This phenomenon is analyzed in the context of dynamical localization, where we identify a quantum regime characterized by strong coupling between the electron, the field, and the electron's own radiation. In this limit, the electron and photon modes become hybridized, forming new eigenstates. We further illustrate that the electron's scattering amplitude exhibits rapid, periodic variations, which serve as the fundamental mechanism for its dynamical stabilization.

While electric actuators are standard in legged robots, their integration of compliance is limited despite the critical role of compliance in biological locomotion. This study introduces a reinforcement learning framework designed to instruct compliant robots by modeling the leg as a series of two actuators with an elastic joint. This architecture mirrors the biological structure of two tendons acting on a single joint, offering a more nuanced approach to compliance. The research demonstrates that this method effectively trains the robot to manage those compliant elements for enhanced mobility. Specifically, the robot achieves a 10% increase in running speed and demonstrates superior adaptability to environmental changes when compared to a fully rigid counterpart.

This study addresses the contentious issue of quantum divisibility, particularly the debate over whether a qubit can be split into two equal halves. To resolve this uncertainty, we introduce a novel variational approach designed to determine if a given quantum state qualifies as an entangled state representing divisibility. This method offers an alternative to traditional entanglement-based criteria specifically for answering the question of divisibility. We demonstrate that every n-level quantum state (qu-nit) can be partitioned into two equal portions. Furthermore, we establish that the boundary condition for an irreducible two-level state is its maximality. Finally, we prove that any non-maximality two-level state can be divided into two halves of equal quality.

Magnetic reconnection is a fundamental process in astrophysical plasmas, often initiating mini-scale tearing modes that subsequently evolve into larger systems. These modes are critical for energy release and particle acceleration, particularly within the solar corona. A key challenge in modeling them lies in the difficulty of directly simulating the kinetic physics of the electron diffusion region (EDR) using global-scale simulations. Consequently, researchers employ simplified one-dimensional slab models that bridge the gap between kinetic theory and astrophysical reality. This work examines the physics of such a model, specifically focusing on the collisionless regime. We analyze the collisionless tearing mode in a slab configuration, emphasizing the role of electron kinetics in the EDR. By employing a hybrid model that combines kinetic treatment of electrons with fluid descriptions of ions, we capture the essential physics of the recombination region while maintaining computational feasibility for larger systems. This approach provides valuable insights into how microscale processes influence macroscopic phenomena, ultimately aiding in the interpretation of observational data from space missions. We introduce a semi-supervised, feature-level trait manipulation framework designed to enhance fashion image retrieval. Rather than operating on raw pixels, our method modifies a specific, learnable representation within a pre-trained autoencoder to alter desired garment attributes—such as color, style, or fit—while leaving other aspects unchanged. By optimizing these manipulation parameters using a dataset of image pairs that differ only in the target trait, we ensure precise and controllable edits. The resulting manipulated features are then employed to train a metric learning model, which generates an image embedding that captures fine-grained visual details. Empirical evaluations on the FashionIQ benchmark demonstrate that our approach significantly boosts accuracy, achieving a 2.8% improvement in mean average precision (mAP) and a 2.1% improvement in recall@100 compared to prior state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a dual-ascent framework designed to resolve a broad range of linear ill-posed problems within the context of Banach spaces. For instances of problem severity characterized by finite index, the dual approach transforms the original issue into a dual problem that remains well-posed. Consequently, the asymptotic convergence of a dual-ascent algorithm applied to this newly formulated problem ensures the convergence of its solution back to that of the initial problem. Furthermore, the work establishes a dual-ascent algorithm specifically for ill-investigated problems that lack a finite index, demonstrating that the associated error bounds are governed by the error of the best linear approximation.

Light field color-to-depth conversion is essential for generating 3D point clouds from hyperspectral images. However, traditional single-channel regression models often fail to capture the complexities of real-world colorimetric data, leading to inaccurate depth estimation. This study introduces a new supervised learning framework designed to enhance these estimation capabilities. The approach employs a multi-channel strategy to analyze RGB color data alongside blue-channel luminance, utilizing convolutional neural networks to identify local color patterns and global luminance characteristics. A key innovation is the implementation of an occlusion-aware mechanism; since real objects frequently cast shadows and are partially blocked, the model discards outputs corresponding to occluded regions to mitigate errors. The final global depth map is synthesized by integrating the regression results from all channels. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in accuracy.

This study introduces a newly derived set of bilinear formulas for the Fokas-Lenells equation, which differ from the established ones by Zhiber and Novikov. The authors present these results using a bilinear approach.

We investigate the holographic duality between non-Riemannian field theories and non-Riemannian geometries, deriving non-Riemannian actions for both the Veitch-Maldacena and Veillette frameworks. These actions are constructed as duals to standard Riemannian gravitational Lagrangians, specifically generalizing the Einstein-Hilbert term. We establish that this non-Hilbert action reduces to the Einstein-Hilbert form in the limit of standard holographic dualities. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this non-Riemannian non-Hilbert term emerges as the dual of the Plebański action when applied to Plebański dark matter.

In multi-access point (AP) or extender-based IEEE 802.11 networks, the performance hinges on the selection of the primary AP or extender. This paper introduces a method leveraging 802.11k/v framework to assess AP/channel loads and the quality of associated links, thereby enabling clients to make informed selections. The proposed mechanism utilizes virtual 802.11v messages to gather load data from all nearby APs or extenders. Furthermore, it enhances the measurement of link quality by incorporating the signal-to-noise ratio alongside the packet error rate. The research demonstrates that the proposed algorithm achieves superior performance relative to existing methods.
